```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Sanchez et al. (2023) built a model-based workflow that starts from in vitro
co-culture data and ends with a recommended clinical dose range for FAP-4-1BBL
(RO7122290), a bispecific fusion protein that costimulates T cells through 4-1BB
only while it is simultaneously bound to fibroblast activation protein (FAP) on
cancer-associated fibroblasts. FAP-4-1BBL is given with the CEA x CD3 T-cell
bispecific cibisatamab, which induces the 4-1BB that FAP-4-1BBL engages. The
paper deposits Monolix code for its Model 1 and two RxODE scripts for the
clinical simulations, and the three packaged models follow that split:

| Model file | What it holds | Paper section |
|---|---|---|
| `Sanchez_2023_ro7122290_invitro` | In vitro co-culture: Model 1 (4-1BB time course, mixed-effects fit), FAP-4-1BBL binding in the well, Model 3 (fold increase in killing), Model 2 (FAP-dependent loss of monotherapy killing) | Models 1-3, Figures 1-3 |
| `Sanchez_2023_ro7122290_qsp` | Clinical dose selection with 4-1BB held at 80 receptors per T cell | Simulation 1, Figure 4 |
| `Sanchez_2023_ro7122290_cibisatamab_qsp` | Clinical combination with cibisatamab PK, cibisatamab-driven 4-1BB (Model 1) and Models 2-3 in the tumor | Simulations 2-3, Figures 5-6 |

```{r models}
ui_vitro <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Sanchez_2023_ro7122290_invitro"))
ui_dose <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Sanchez_2023_ro7122290_qsp"))
ui_combo <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Sanchez_2023_ro7122290_cibisatamab_qsp"))
```

* Citation: `r ui_vitro$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.13065>
* Supplementary information (Supplementary Materials and Methods, Table S1,
  Monolix and RxODE code): Data S1 of the article.

# Population

No patients were fitted. The pharmacodynamics come from three in vitro
experiments in which MKN-45 gastric cancer cells (high CEACAM5) were co-cultured
with human PBMC effector cells at an effector:target ratio of 1:1 and with
fibroblasts expressing FAP (Supplementary Materials and Methods):

* Experiment 1 (Model 1): cibisatamab 0, 0.2, 2, 20, 200 and 2000 nM, or 20 nM
  with 1 nM FAP-4-1BBL, fibroblasts at 92,000 FAP/fibroblast; 4-1BB per CD8+ T
  cell measured at 4, 21, 45 and 69 h.
* Experiment 2 (Model 3): 2 nM cibisatamab with FAP-4-1BBL 0 to 10,000 nM,
  fibroblasts at 92,000 (high) or 12,700 (low) FAP/fibroblast; tumor cell
  killing imaged for up to 138 h.
* Experiment 3 (Model 2): 0.2 nM cibisatamab with 0 to 100% of the
  fibroblasts expressing 6,800 FAP/fibroblast.

The clinical simulations use virtual colorectal carcinoma patients: the
FAP-4-1BBL population PK of Micallef et al. (ACoP 2020) and an internal
cibisatamab PK model, both tabulated in Table S1, with FAP expression from
published immunohistochemistry H-scores (median 12% FAP-positive fibroblasts,
12,000 FAP/fibroblast).

```{r population}
str(ui_combo$population)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries a trailing comment naming its source. Summary:

| Quantity | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `lemax`, `lec50`, `lhill` | 537.682 receptors/cell, 16.004 nM, 0.210 | Table 2; Table S1 for the extra decimals |
| `lsignal2`, `lt_stop` | 381.92 receptors/cell, 16.18 h | Table 2; Table S1 |
| `lktr`, `lkin`, `lkout` | 0.2801 1/h, 2.952 receptors/cell/h, 0.2832 1/h | Table 2; Table S1 |
| Model 1 random effects | SD 0.1 held constant; SD 0.09 on `ktr` | Table 2 |
| `addSd` | 5.36 receptors/cell | Table 2 |
| `kill_max`, `trimer50`, `hill_kill`, `kill_base` | 4.37, 3.91e-3, 1.16, 1.04 | Table 3 (Model 3) |
| `kill_nofap`, `kill_maxdec`, `hill_fap`, `logit_fap50` | 101.9%, 67.4%, 0.86, -1.1 | Table 3 (Model 2) |
| `kd_fap`, `koff_fap`, `kd_41bb`, `koff_41bb` | 0.7 nM, 0.1 1/h, 0.2 nM, 0.1 1/h | Table S1 (`kon = koff / KD`) |
| FAP-4-1BBL `lvc`, `lvp`, `lcl`, `lq` | 3.77 L, 0.83 L, 0.0154 L/h, 0.0219 L/h | Table S1 (volumes in mL in the deposited code) |
| FAP-4-1BBL `lvmax`, `lkm` | 0.455 mg/h, 5.18 mg/L | Table S1; mg/h from the deposited code (see Assumptions) |
| FAP-4-1BBL IIV | V1-CL block (0.485, 0.04, 0.104); V2 1.52; Vmax-Km block (0.306, 0.365, 0.798) | Deposited dose-selection code |
| Cibisatamab `lvc_`, `lvp_`, `lcl_`, `lq_cibisatamab` | 3.95 L, 4.38 L, 0.063 L/h, 0.039 L/h | Table S1 |
| `ktum_in`, `ktum_out` | 0.06, 0.137 1/h (2.2:1); 0.03, 0.3 1/h (10:1) | Table S1 |
| `mw`, `mw_cibisatamab` | 177,000 and 194,000 g/mol | Deposited code (`/0.177`, `*5.1546`) |
| Tumor geometry, cell density, fibroblast fraction, E:T, T-cell fraction | 50 mm ellipsoid, 1e7 cells/cm^3, 0.15, 0.1, 40% x 0.4 | Deposited RxODE code |
| `fap_per_fib`, `fap_pos_pct` (clinic) | 12,000, 12% | Supplementary Materials and Methods, Simulation 1 |
| `r41bb_tcell` | 80 receptors per T cell | Supplementary Materials and Methods, Simulation 1 |
| Step function, Signal, transit chain, 4-1BB turnover | Equations 1-8 and 10-16 | Results, Model 1 and Model 3 |
| Binding ODEs and FAP initial condition | Equations 17-22 | Results, Model 3 |
| Receptor occupancy and trimers per cell | Equations 23-26 | Results, Model 3 |
| Fold increase in killing; monotherapy killing | Equations 27 and 9 | Results, Models 3 and 2 |

# Model 1: 4-1BB expression on CD8+ T cells in vitro

Typical-value 4-1BB trajectories for every Experiment 1 condition, overlaid on
the observed medians read off the individual-fit panels of Figure S4 by the
maintainers.

```{r model1}
conds <- tibble(
  cond = c("No TCB", "0.2 nM", "2 nM", "20 nM", "20 nM + FAP-4-1BBL 1 nM", "200 nM", "2000 nM"),
  cibi = c(0, 0.2, 2, 20, 20, 200, 2000),
  fap41bbl = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0)
) |>
  mutate(id = row_number())

ev_m1 <- bind_rows(
  conds |> filter(fap41bbl > 0) |>
    transmute(id, time = 0, amt = fap41bbl, evid = 1, cmt = "medium"),
  conds |> tidyr::crossing(time = seq(0, 72, by = 1)) |>
    transmute(id, time, amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "expr_41bb")
) |>
  left_join(conds |> select(id, CONC_CIBISATAMAB_NM = cibi), by = "id") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim_m1 <- rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(ui_vitro), ev_m1, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  left_join(conds |> select(id, cond), by = "id")

obs_m1 <- tribble(
  ~cond, ~time, ~obs,
  "No TCB", 4, 16.3, "No TCB", 21, 8.2, "No TCB", 45, 23.8, "No TCB", 69, -1,
  "0.2 nM", 4, 9.5, "0.2 nM", 21, 27.5, "0.2 nM", 45, 67.5, "0.2 nM", 69, 0.8,
  "2 nM", 4, 10, "2 nM", 21, 64.5, "2 nM", 45, 63, "2 nM", 69, 0.5,
  "20 nM", 4, 14, "20 nM", 21, 56, "20 nM", 45, 107, "20 nM", 69, 7,
  "20 nM + FAP-4-1BBL 1 nM", 4, 14, "20 nM + FAP-4-1BBL 1 nM", 21, 93,
  "20 nM + FAP-4-1BBL 1 nM", 45, 143, "20 nM + FAP-4-1BBL 1 nM", 69, 17,
  "200 nM", 4, 9, "200 nM", 21, 141, "200 nM", 45, 89, "200 nM", 69, 3,
  "2000 nM", 4, 10, "2000 nM", 21, 71, "2000 nM", 45, 173, "2000 nM", 69, 1
)

ggplot(sim_m1, aes(time, expr_41bb)) +
  geom_line(colour = "purple") +
  geom_point(data = obs_m1, aes(time, obs), colour = "steelblue") +
  facet_wrap(~ factor(cond, levels = conds$cond), scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "4-1BB receptors per CD8+ T cell",
       caption = "Typical-value predictions; points read off Figure S4 of Sanchez 2023.")
```

```{r model1-check}
m1_cmp <- obs_m1 |>
  filter(time %in% c(21, 45), cond != "No TCB") |>
  left_join(sim_m1 |> select(cond, time, pred = expr_41bb), by = c("cond", "time"))
knitr::kable(m1_cmp, digits = 1)
# The combination condition is fitted through Signal2, which is 39% above the
# monotherapy Signal at the same 20 nM cibisatamab.
sig_ratio <- exp(ui_vitro$theta["lsignal2"]) /
  (exp(ui_vitro$theta["lemax"]) * 20^exp(ui_vitro$theta["lhill"]) /
     (20^exp(ui_vitro$theta["lhill"]) + exp(ui_vitro$theta["lec50"])^exp(ui_vitro$theta["lhill"])))
sig_ratio
stopifnot(
  abs(sig_ratio - 1.39) < 0.01,
  # Typical predictions sit within the individual-fit scatter of the medians.
  median(abs(m1_cmp$pred - m1_cmp$obs) / m1_cmp$obs) < 0.35
)
```

# Model 3: trimeric complexes and tumor cell killing in vitro

Experiment 2 conditions: 2 nM cibisatamab, 10,000 fibroblasts in 200 uL, and
FAP-4-1BBL added at time zero. The trimeric complexes per T cell are averaged
over 0-120 h before entering the Emax model (Equation 27).

```{r model3-grid}
grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  fap_per_fib = 10^seq(2, log10(5e5), length.out = 30),
  conc = 10^seq(-3, 3, length.out = 31)
) |>
  mutate(id = row_number())

ev_grid <- bind_rows(
  grid |> transmute(id, time = 0, amt = conc, evid = 1, cmt = "medium"),
  grid |> transmute(id, time = 120, amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "trimer")
) |>
  mutate(CONC_CIBISATAMAB_NM = 2) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim_grid <- rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(ui_vitro), ev_grid,
  params = grid |> select(id, fap_per_fib),
  returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  select(id, trimer_avg) |>
  left_join(grid, by = "id")

ggplot(sim_grid, aes(fap_per_fib, conc, fill = log10(trimer_avg))) +
  geom_raster(interpolate = TRUE) +
  geom_contour(aes(z = trimer_avg), breaks = 2.6e-2, colour = "red") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 13400, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "plasma") +
  labs(x = "FAP per fibroblast", y = "FAP-4-1BBL (nM)", fill = "log10 trimers\nper T cell",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 3c of Sanchez 2023; red contour = 2.6e-2 trimeric complexes per T cell.")
```

The paper quotes three points on the 2.6e-2 contour (90% of the maximum fold
increase): the minimum of 13,400 FAP/fibroblast reached only at 0.37 nM, and the
range 0.01-11.5 nM at 100,000 FAP/fibroblast.

```{r model3-points}
fig3c <- tibble(
  fap_per_fib = c(13400, 1e5, 1e5),
  conc = c(0.37, 0.0115, 11.5),
  id = 1:3
)
ev3 <- bind_rows(
  fig3c |> transmute(id, time = 0, amt = conc, evid = 1, cmt = "medium"),
  fig3c |> transmute(id, time = 120, amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "trimer")
) |>
  mutate(CONC_CIBISATAMAB_NM = 2) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
pts <- rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(ui_vitro), ev3, params = fig3c |> select(id, fap_per_fib),
               returnType = "data.frame") |>
  select(id, trimer_avg) |>
  left_join(fig3c, by = "id") |>
  mutate(published = 2.6e-2, pct_diff = 100 * (trimer_avg / published - 1))
pts |>
  select(fap_per_fib, conc, trimer_avg, published, pct_diff) |>
  dplyr::rename("FAP per fibroblast" = fap_per_fib, "FAP-4-1BBL (nM)" = conc,
                "Simulated trimers per T cell" = trimer_avg,
                "Figure 3c" = published, "% difference" = pct_diff) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4)
# Deterministic typical-value solve: the binding constants, Model 1 and the
# Signal2/Signal ratio fix these values exactly.
stopifnot(all(abs(pts$pct_diff) < 10))
```

Fold increase in killing over the Experiment 2 concentration range (the bell
shape of Figure 3a, observed means read off the figure by the maintainers):

```{r model3-bell}
bell <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  fap = c(High = 92000, Low = 12700),
  conc = c(0, 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100, 1000, 10000)
) |>
  mutate(level = rep(c("High FAP", "Low FAP"), each = 8), id = row_number())
ev_bell <- bind_rows(
  bell |> filter(conc > 0) |> transmute(id, time = 0, amt = conc, evid = 1, cmt = "medium"),
  bell |> transmute(id, time = 120, amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "trimer")
) |>
  mutate(CONC_CIBISATAMAB_NM = 2) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
sim_bell <- rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(ui_vitro), ev_bell,
                    params = bell |> select(id, fap_per_fib = fap),
                    returnType = "data.frame") |>
  select(id, fold_kill) |>
  left_join(bell |> select(id, level, conc), by = "id") |>
  mutate(obs = c(1.0, 3.8, 4.2, 4.3, 4.45, 2.45, 1.45, 1.0,
                 1.05, 2.0, 3.75, 4.1, 2.45, 1.6, 1.15, 1.0))
ggplot(sim_bell, aes(pmax(conc, 1e-3), fold_kill, colour = level)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point(aes(y = obs), shape = 1, size = 2) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "FAP-4-1BBL (nM; 0 plotted at 1e-3)", y = "Fold increase vs cibisatamab alone",
       caption = "Lines: model at 120 h; open circles: means read off Figure 3a.")
stopifnot(
  # The bell shape: the 10,000 nM fold increase is back near the monotherapy level.
  all(sim_bell$fold_kill[sim_bell$conc == 10000] < 1.6),
  max(sim_bell$fold_kill) > 4
)
```

# Model 2: cibisatamab monotherapy killing versus FAP-positive fibroblasts

```{r model2}
m2 <- tibble(fap_pos_pct = c(0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 40, 60, 100), id = seq_len(8))
ev_m2 <- m2 |>
  transmute(id, time = 0, amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "trimer", CONC_CIBISATAMAB_NM = 0.2)
sim_m2 <- rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(ui_vitro), ev_m2, params = m2, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  select(id, kill_mono_pct) |>
  left_join(m2, by = "id")
sim_m2 |>
  select(fap_pos_pct, kill_mono_pct) |>
  dplyr::rename("FAP-positive fibroblasts (%)" = fap_pos_pct,
                "Monotherapy killing (% of 0% FAP)" = kill_mono_pct) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
stopifnot(
  abs(sim_m2$kill_mono_pct[1] - 100) < 2,  # Figure 2a dashed line at 0%
  abs(sim_m2$kill_mono_pct[8] - 34.6) < 1  # Figure 2a dashed line at 100%
)
```

# Simulation 1: dose selection for maximum trimeric complex formation

Area under the trimeric-complex curve (`trimer_per_tcell`) over 30 weeks of
FAP-4-1BBL infused over 2 h q1w, q2w or q3w, for 100 virtual patients with IIV
on the FAP-4-1BBL PK only, under the 2.2:1 and 10:1 plasma:tumor distribution
scenarios. The same 100 random-effect draws are reused at every dose so the
dose-response curve is not confounded by resampling.

```{r sim1}
set.seed(20231)
n_pat <- 100
om <- ui_dose$omega
draws <- matrix(rnorm(n_pat * nrow(om)), n_pat) %*% chol(om)
colnames(draws) <- colnames(om)
draws <- as.data.frame(draws)

doses <- c(1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 14, 21, 30, 45, 67, 100, 145)
scen <- tibble(
  scenario = c("2.2:1", "10:1"),
  ktum_in = c(0.06, 0.03),
  ktum_out = c(0.137, 0.3)
)
t_end <- 24 * 7 * 30
trap <- function(x, y) sum(diff(x) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)

auc_one <- function(dose, weeks, s) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = dose, rate = dose / 2, ii = weeks * 168,
                   until = t_end - 1, cmt = "central") |>
    rxode2::et(seq(0, t_end, by = 2))
  prm <- cbind(draws, ktum_in = s$ktum_in, ktum_out = s$ktum_out)
  # One shared event table with one params row per patient: rxSolve labels
  # the patients `sim.id`.
  out <- rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(ui_dose), ev, params = prm, returnType = "data.frame")
  out |>
    group_by(id = sim.id) |>
    summarise(auc = trap(time, trimer_per_tcell), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(dose = dose, schedule = paste0("q", weeks, "w"), scenario = s$scenario)
}

sim1 <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(scen)), function(i) {
  bind_rows(lapply(1:3, function(w) bind_rows(lapply(doses, auc_one, weeks = w, s = scen[i, ]))))
}))

sum1 <- sim1 |>
  group_by(scenario, schedule, dose) |>
  summarise(p05 = quantile(auc, 0.05), p25 = quantile(auc, 0.25), med = median(auc),
            p75 = quantile(auc, 0.75), p95 = quantile(auc, 0.95), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(sum1, aes(dose, med, colour = scenario, fill = scenario)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p25), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(aes(y = p75), linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~schedule) +
  labs(x = "FAP-4-1BBL dose (mg)", y = "AUC of trimeric complexes per T cell (x h)",
       colour = "Plasma:tumor", fill = "Plasma:tumor",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Sanchez 2023 (median, 25th-75th and 5th-95th percentiles).")
```

```{r sim1-check}
opt <- sum1 |>
  group_by(scenario, schedule) |>
  slice_max(med, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(scenario, schedule, sim_opt = dose) |>
  left_join(
    tribble(
      ~scenario, ~schedule, ~paper_opt, ~paper_lo, ~paper_hi,
      "2.2:1", "q1w", 3, 2, 10,
      "2.2:1", "q2w", 10, 4, 31,
      "2.2:1", "q3w", 21, 7, 65,
      "10:1", "q1w", 11, 5, 31,
      "10:1", "q2w", 33, 14, 80,
      "10:1", "q3w", 67, 23, 145
    ),
    by = c("scenario", "schedule")
  )
opt |>
  dplyr::rename("Plasma:tumor" = scenario, "Schedule" = schedule,
                "Simulated optimum (mg)" = sim_opt, "Figure 4 optimum (mg)" = paper_opt,
                "Figure 4 range low (mg)" = paper_lo, "Figure 4 range high (mg)" = paper_hi) |>
  knitr::kable()
# The median dose-response is flat near its peak, so the simulated optimum is
# checked against the paper's within-20%-of-maximum dose range rather than
# against the single optimum dose.
stopifnot(all(opt$sim_opt >= opt$paper_lo & opt$sim_opt <= opt$paper_hi))
```

The optimum doses agree with Figure 4. The simulated AUC is several-fold higher
than the Figure 4 axis (largest median here `r round(max(sum1$med))` versus
about 100 in the paper); see Assumptions and deviations.

# Simulation 2: tumor FAP expression and the expected benefit

Typical-value simulation over the first 120 h: cibisatamab 100 mg over 2 h,
then FAP-4-1BBL over 2 h at the 2.75 mg dose that maximizes trimeric complex
formation in this window, or at a dose 100-fold higher. FAP expression varies
over a grid of FAP-positive fibroblast percentages at the median 12,000
FAP/fibroblast.

```{r sim2}
grid2 <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  dose = c(2.75, 275),
  fap_pos_pct = c(1, 2, 5, 10, 15, 25, 40, 60, 80, 100)
) |>
  mutate(id = row_number())
ev2 <- bind_rows(
  grid2 |> transmute(id, time = 0, amt = 100, rate = 50, evid = 1, cmt = "central_cibisatamab"),
  grid2 |> transmute(id, time = 2, amt = dose, rate = dose / 2, evid = 1, cmt = "central"),
  grid2 |> transmute(id, time = 120, amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "central")
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
sim2 <- rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(ui_combo), ev2, params = grid2 |> select(id, fap_pos_pct),
                returnType = "data.frame") |>
  select(id, trimer_avg, fold_kill, kill_abs) |>
  left_join(grid2, by = "id")

sim2 |>
  select(dose, fap_pos_pct, trimer_avg, fold_kill, kill_abs) |>
  pivot_longer(c(trimer_avg, fold_kill, kill_abs)) |>
  mutate(name = factor(name, c("trimer_avg", "fold_kill", "kill_abs"),
                       c("Average trimers per T cell", "Fold increase vs monotherapy",
                         "Killing vs monotherapy without FAP+"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(fap_pos_pct, value, colour = factor(dose))) +
  geom_line() + geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "FAP-positive fibroblasts in tumor (%)", y = NULL, colour = "Dose (mg)",
       caption = "Typical-value counterpart of Figure 5 of Sanchez 2023.")
```

```{r sim2-check}
hi <- sim2 |> filter(dose == 2.75)
stopifnot(
  # Figure 5: at the trimer-maximizing dose the fold increase is near its
  # maximum once a few percent of the fibroblasts express FAP ...
  all(hi$fold_kill[hi$fap_pos_pct >= 10] > 4),
  # ... while absolute killing falls with more FAP-positive fibroblasts.
  hi$kill_abs[hi$fap_pos_pct == 100] < hi$kill_abs[hi$fap_pos_pct == 10],
  # A 100-fold higher dose forms far fewer trimers.
  all(sim2$trimer_avg[sim2$dose == 275] < hi$trimer_avg)
)
```

Simulation 3 (Figure 6) layers permutation tests over Simulation 2-type
virtual patients to size dose-ranging cohorts; it is a statistical design
exercise over the same model and is not reproduced here.

# FAP-4-1BBL plasma PK (PKNCA)

The paper reports no NCA; the block below documents the single-dose typical
exposure implied by the Table S1 parameters for three doses near the
Simulation 1 optima.

```{r pknca}
ev_pk <- tibble(dose_mg = c(3, 10, 21), id = 1:3)
ev_pk <- bind_rows(
  ev_pk |> transmute(id, dose_mg, time = 0, amt = dose_mg, rate = dose_mg / 2, evid = 1, cmt = "central"),
  ev_pk |> tidyr::crossing(time = c(0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24, 48, 72, 96, 168, 336, 504)) |>
    transmute(id, dose_mg, time, amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "central")
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
sim_pk <- rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(ui_dose), ev_pk, returnType = "data.frame")
conc <- sim_pk |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc) |>
  left_join(distinct(ev_pk, id, dose_mg), by = "id")
dose_df <- ev_pk |> filter(evid == 1) |> select(id, dose_mg, time, amt)
o_conc <- PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | dose_mg + id)
o_dose <- PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | dose_mg + id, route = "intravascular", duration = 2)
o_data <- PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose,
                    intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                                           aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE))
nca <- pk.nca(o_data)
as.data.frame(nca$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  select(dose_mg, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::rename("Dose (mg)" = dose_mg, "Cmax (mg/L)" = cmax, "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
                "AUC0-inf (mg*h/L)" = aucinf.obs, "t1/2 (h)" = half.life) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Vmax units.** Table S1 prints Vmax as 0.455 ug/h, but the deposited
  dose-selection code subtracts `Vmax * C / (C + Km)` from an amount in mg with
  concentrations in mg/L, so Vmax is 0.455 mg/h. Only the mg/h reading puts the
  Simulation 1 optimum doses where Figure 4 has them (with 0.455 ug/h the
  nonlinear clearance is negligible and every optimum moves several-fold lower).
  The volumes and clearances are in mL and mL/h in the code (Table S1 labels V1
  and V2 in L); they are packaged as 3.77 L, 0.83 L, 0.0154 L/h and 0.0219 L/h.
* **Signal under FAP-4-1BBL costimulation.** The deposited clinical code
  multiplies the monotherapy Signal by an added value, capped at SignalMAX. The
  in vitro model sets that multiplier to Signal2 divided by the monotherapy
  Signal at 20 nM cibisatamab (1.39, the "39% increase in Signal" of the
  Supplementary Materials and Methods) whenever FAP-4-1BBL is in the well, which
  reproduces Equation 3 at the tested condition and the Figure 3c contour. The
  clinical combination model keeps the code default `added_value = 1`; the
  paper describes the clinical increase only as proportional to the trimeric
  complex formation, without a usable form.
* **4-1BB binding form.** Equation 16 degrades only the free 4-1BB, but the
  deposited code lets the total 4-1BB pool follow the per-cell turnover of
  Model 1 and redistributes it by binding. The packaged models use the code
  form: it puts the in vitro trimer maximum at 0.37 nM as Figure 3c does, while
  the Equation 16 form moves it to about 1 nM. Equation 17 also prints
  `koff_FAP x FAP-4-1BBL` where the code (and mass balance) has
  `koff_FAP x Trimeric`; the code form is used.
* **Stop time in the clinic.** Signal and basal 4-1BB synthesis switch off
  16.2 h after the first cibisatamab dose, so the cibisatamab combination model
  is meaningful over the 120-h and one-week windows of Simulations 2 and 3, not
  for multi-cycle regimens. Simulation 1 uses the separate constant-4-1BB model.
  In the in vitro model basal synthesis continues in cibisatamab-free wells, as
  the deposited Monolix code specifies.
* **T-cell count.** The deposited dose-selection code initializes 4-1BB from
  `E_T_ratio / 100` T cells per tumor cell but normalizes trimers by
  `E_T_ratio x 40% x 0.4`; both packaged clinical models use the latter
  throughout. The 4-1BB concentration is about 1e-5 nM either way, far below the
  FAP and drug concentrations, so the choice does not move the results. The in
  vitro model applies the same 40% x 0.4 T-cell factors to the PBMC count, which
  the paper does not state for the wells; the receptor concentration is again
  negligible against FAP and drug.
* **Clinical FAP expression.** Simulation 1 fixes FAP at 12% FAP-positive
  fibroblasts and 12,000 FAP/fibroblast as stated in the Supplementary Materials
  and Methods. The deposited code takes these medians from an H-score script
  that is not part of the supplement. With the stated medians the simulated
  trimeric-complex AUC is about seven-fold above the Figure 4 axis; trimer
  formation is linear in FAP at these receptor levels, so the optimum doses are
  unaffected while the absolute AUC is. Simulation 2 here uses a deterministic
  FAP grid instead of the H-score sampling.
* **Cibisatamab tumor distribution.** Table S1 lists the same 0.06 and 0.137 1/h
  rate constants for cibisatamab (labelled a 2.5:1 ratio) as for FAP-4-1BBL;
  the deposited code shares them between the two drugs.
* **Model 1 parameter values.** Table 2 and Table S1 are used. The parameter
  block of the deposited Monolix project holds slightly different values
  (for example EC50 13.6 nM, residual SD 7.25), which are the starting values of
  a later run rather than the reported estimates.
* **Observed Model 1 values** in the first figure were read by eye off Figure
  S4; Figure 3a means likewise. They are qualitative comparators.
